title: How a RAG Chatbot Answers From Your Docs
subtitle: Turn MkDocs into a chat assistant that cites what it read
intro: Your MkDocs site knows every answer, but users still ask the chatbot and get made-up replies. What if it could look things up first?
takeaway: RAG makes the chatbot retrieve real doc chunks before it writes, so answers stay grounded in your docs.

sections.heading: Analogy: a librarian with sticky notes
sections.body:
Imagine a librarian who answers questions by first pulling sticky notes from books, then writing the answer using only those notes.

A RAG pipeline does the same. RAG means Retrieval-Augmented Generation: retrieve relevant text, then generate an answer. Vector storage means turning text into numbers (embeddings) so similar meanings sit close together.

Obelisk does this for MkDocs: it indexes your docs, stores embeddings in ChromaDB, and watches for changes in real time.

That setup explains why you would add retrieval at all.

sections.heading: Why does this exist?: stop hallucinating, start citing
sections.body:
A plain LLM guesses from memory. A RAG system grounds it in your docs.

Obelisk's flow is: document processing -> embedding via Ollama or OpenAI -> vector storage in ChromaDB -> retrieval -> generation via Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible API. You get a drop-in OpenAI-compatible endpoint and Docker deployment.

Example: you ask "how to install?" It retrieves the Installation chunk with "poetry install" and Python 3.12+ prerequisites, then answers with those steps.

Grounding helps, but the retrieval step can still fail.

sections.heading: What can go wrong?: when retrieval misses
sections.body:
If indexing is stale, answers cite old docs. Obelisk adds real-time document monitoring to re-index on change.

Other failures:
- Bad chunking splits an answer across two notes, so nothing matches well.
- Wrong embeddings make "install" look like "uninstall".
- Too few retrieved chunks starves the LLM; too many drowns it with noise.

Fix by testing retrieval first, then generation.

steps.narration: Start with your MkDocs markdown files as the source of truth.
Split docs into chunks and turn each into a vector embedding.
Save vectors in ChromaDB for fast similarity search.
User asks a question via the OpenAI-compatible API.
Embed the question and pull the closest doc chunks.
Ollama generates the answer using only those retrieved chunks.

quiz.q: What does RAG do first when you ask a question?
options: Generates an answer from memory, then searches docs
Retrieves relevant doc chunks, then generates an answer
Retrains the LLM on your MkDocs site
quiz.why: RAG = Retrieval-Augmented Generation: retrieve grounded context, then generate.

quiz.q: What fails first if usage grows 100x?
options: ChromaDB retrieval slows and embeddings cost spikes
quiz.why: Vector search and embedding generation become bottlenecks under high query volume.

quiz.q: Why use an OpenAI-compatible API in Obelisk?
options: To let existing OpenAI clients point to your local RAG without code changes
To remove need for vector storage
quiz.why: It acts as a drop-in replacement so apps can use local Ollama-backed RAG easily.
